groups.rationale: Two exact duplicate clusters support one portable accessibility audit and repair workflow; the inspected ui-styling and d3-viz contexts remain source distinctions, not separate capabilities.
groups.authorityEffectRiskBoundary: May inspect and recommend or implement bounded interface accessibility repairs on user-provided artifacts; no authority to certify legal conformance, alter unrelated product behavior, or act against external systems.
groups.proofLimits: Cluster evidence proves reviewed intent and duplicate equivalence only; implementation quality, WCAG conformance, assistive-technology coverage, and live-browser behavior require capability-specific evaluation.

groups.rationale: Repeated reviews converge on a portable lifecycle of test-first work, independent review, and evidence-backed completion; duplicates are consolidated without merging domain-specific verification procedures.
groups.authorityEffectRiskBoundary: May plan and report bounded verification gates, request or process review evidence, and block completion claims until supplied checks pass; no authority to declare safety, compliance, security, or production readiness without independent evidence.
groups.proofLimits: Cluster evidence does not prove live tests, reviewer independence, or semantic interpretation of results; downstream capability tests and human or domain review remain required.

groups.rationale: These reviewed workflows form one reusable planning and handoff spine already represented by forge; finance, legal, provider, and task-specific orchestration candidates remain outside the group.
groups.authorityEffectRiskBoundary: May structure plans, bounded delegation, evidence handoffs, skill discovery, execution checkpoints, and branch-finish decisions; no authority to create external commitments, bypass consent, or execute delegated actions without explicit authorization.
groups.proofLimits: Reviews prove stated workflow contracts only; they do not prove scheduler behavior, agent reliability, conflict resolution, or successful execution in a target environment.
